cards.text: This letter skips the hello and jumps straight in. The writer never signs his name, but he's writing to people he calls “you,” about “That which was from the beginning.” And friend, he talks like a man who was THERE.

cards.question: The writer says he only heard about this from other people, secondhand.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Secondhand? NO sir. He heard it, SAW it with his own eyes, gazed at it, TOUCHED it with his own hands, and he calls it the Word of life.
That life was revealed. The eternal life that was with the Father stepped out where the writer and the others with him could actually see it.

cards.question: The writer and the others with him have seen this eternal life up close. What do they do with it?

answers.text: They testify to it and proclaim it
They keep it quiet among themselves
They wait for the right time to share it

cards.question: The writer and the others with him proclaim what they've seen and heard to the readers. Why?

answers.text: So the readers can have fellowship with them
So the readers can earn a place among them
So the readers can prove they are worthy

cards.text: And this isn't some little fan club for the folks who got front-row seats. This fellowship goes WAY higher than that.

cards.question: Who does the writer say this fellowship of theirs is with?

answers.text: The Father and His Son Jesus Christ
The prophets and the holy angels
The elders and the apostles

cards.question: The writer gives one more reason he and the others write these things. What is it?

answers.text: So that our joy may be complete
So that our names will be remembered
So that our worries may be settled

cards.text: Now the writer gets to the message they heard from Him, the BIG one. And he doesn't make you dig for it like scissors in a junk drawer. He puts it right up front.

cards.question: God is ___, and in Him there is no darkness at all.

answers.text: light
distant
silent

cards.text: So say we claim fellowship with God but keep walking in the darkness. That's me swearing I never touched the dough, with dough ALL over my mustache.

cards.question: What does the writer say about us if we claim fellowship with God but walk in the darkness?

answers.text: We lie and don't practice the truth
We are still growing into the truth
We are safe as long as we believe

cards.question: But when we walk in the light as God is in the light, what cleanses us from all sin?

answers.text: The blood of Jesus His Son
The water of the Jordan River
The ashes of a red heifer

cards.question: The writer says that when we walk in the light, we have fellowship with one another.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Next up: saying we have no sin at all. Friend, I shared a junk drawer with dead batteries who SWORE they still had a charge, so I've heard this one before.

cards.question: If we say we have no sin, who does the writer say we're fooling?

answers.text: Ourselves
Our neighbors
Our leaders

cards.text: But there's a better road, and it starts with owning up. Like me walking out holding the burnt tray: “Yeah. That was me.”

cards.question: If we confess our sins, what does the writer say God does?

answers.text: He forgives us and cleanses us
He forgives us but keeps a record
He waits until we prove ourselves

cards.question: The writer comes back to the claim one more time. If we say we have not sinned, what do we make God out to be?

answers.text: A liar
A stranger
A bystander

cards.text: Then he goes soft and calls them “My little children.” He's writing so they won't sin, but if anyone does, they are NOT on their own.

cards.question: When anyone does sin, who does the writer say is our advocate before the Father?

answers.text: Jesus Christ the Righteous One
Moses the servant of God
Michael the archangel

cards.text: And Jesus doesn't just speak up for us. He Himself is the atoning sacrifice for our sins.

cards.question: The writer says Jesus is the atoning sacrifice only for the sins of the people this letter is written to.

answers.text: True
False

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 1 quotes "That which was from the beginning.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 12 quotes "My little children.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card ends with 'he talks like a man who was THERE.' That gives away the answer to card 2, which asks whether the writer only heard about this secondhand.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The card says the writer is writing to people he calls “you,” but 'you' first appears in 1 John 1:2 and 1:3. The card cites only 1 John 1:1.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The setup says this isn't a fan club for 'the folks who got front-row seats' and that the fellowship goes 'WAY higher than that.' This rules out card 8's wrong answer 'The elders and the apostles,' since those are the front-row people.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Stop 1 has almost no humor. Cards 3 and 4 read as plain retelling, and the one joke (the fan club line, card 7) is mild. Papa Dorin reads like a nice dad being pleasant, not laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences. Only the opening card may have up to 3.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke compares the claim to Papa Dorin swearing he never touched the dough while covered in it. That is plainly a lie, so it gives away card 4's answer, 'We lie and don't practice the truth.'

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The question says 'But when we walk in the light,' but the text says 'But if we walk in the light' (1 John 1:7). The 'if' was changed to 'when.'
The question says 'When anyone does sin,' but the text says 'But if anyone does sin' (1 John 2:1). The 'if' was changed to 'when.'
